newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercials, CBOT soybeans.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercials, CBOT soybeans.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended higher on commercial demand and on gains in CBOT soybeans, traders said.

"UGG bought July for the Japanese at the close, RBC-DS bought November while Pioneer and the Pools sold hedges in the November," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to -1.61 Friday from -4.60 Thursday. July-Nov spread $38, July Aug $2.
Japan bought 5,000-6,000 tonnes cash canola overnight, sources said.
CBOT soybean futures touched the 30-cent per bushel upper limit in morning trade, buoyed by tight stocks. July soybean futures closed 13-1/2 cents higher at $8.54-1/2 a bushel.
July canola ended up $0.70 at $404.60 and November settled $0.70 higher at $365.
July flax closed up $2.60 as European buyers bought 6,000 to 10,000 tonnes, traders said.
July western barley ended up $0.30 at $131.60 and October rose $0.20 to $133.50 as PCTS sold, floor sources said.
July feed wheat rose $0.20 to $155.70, October fell $0.20 to $158.20 on commercial trade.
RBC-DS sold December feedpeas down US$1 to a new low of US$182 while Louis Dreyfus bought February down US$0.30 at a new low of US$180, traders said.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
